A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RL Tango study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing content can be matched reliably despite the added appendix and resulting renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original generator evaluations, ProcessBench verifier results, and last-letter concatenation experiments in Section 4, Tables 1–3, and Figure 4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Llama-based training and evaluation results in Appendix C, Table 4.

M1.justification: The interleaved training procedure, rewards, advantage calculations, verifier reweighting, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The new discussion of separate normalization and alpha decay explains choices already specified in v1.

E1.justification: Training datasets, five mathematical benchmarks, four out-of-domain tasks, ProcessBench, and last-letter concatenation coverage are retained. The Llama experiment reuses existing mathematical benchmarks without adding tasks or data domains.

E2.justification: New Table 4 includes an unmodified Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct control alongside Llama-SFT and vanilla GRPO in the added training comparison. Table 1 lacked an unmodified-model control. Comparator membership in the existing tables and Figure 3 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds a configuration using Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct for both generator and verifier, explicitly following Table 1's training and evaluation protocol. Settings for the retained Qwen experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a check of whether TANGO's gains depend on the Qwen model family, reporting results with Llama-based agents. The existing frozen-generator and frozen-verifier ablations, distribution-shift setup, and generation examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version changes reported run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimation, or significance testing. Existing plotted shading is retained, and Table 4 introduces point estimates without additional uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and all four figures retain their results. New Table 4 reports Llama mathematical averages of 25.1% for GRPO and 28.8% for GRPO with TANGO, including MATH500 scores of 56.2% and 60.5%. Section 3.2 also newly reports a qualitative stability advantage from separate advantage normalization.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9), mathematical definitions, and Algorithm 1 are retained. The new normalization rationale is explanatory prose, without a new formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about interleaved RL, outcome-only verifier supervision, mutual reinforcement, and benchmark performance. The Llama results add support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 adds an explanation that merging rewards before normalization can cause scale mismatch and unstable learning. Appendix C interprets the Llama results as evidence that effectiveness extends across model families. No substantive new limitations are introduced.

D1.justification: Appendix C specifies the exact Llama checkpoint for both model roles and states that Table 1's protocol is reused. Existing hyperparameters, implementation instructions, prompts, Algorithm 1, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: All 67 references and the related-work discussion are retained. Positioning against PRIME, supervised reward models, and prior generative verifiers remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short design-choice discussion and Appendix C, relabels the original examples appendix from C to D, updates cross-references, and replaces the preprint footer with NeurIPS 2025 information. The remaining narrative is substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 4 and reflows existing material, including relocating Table 3 and Figure 4 to later pages. The original figures and table contents are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: Appendix C modestly strengthens the evidence beyond v1's Qwen-based TANGO experiments by showing gains with Llama-based agents. Section 3.2 also explains existing training choices more clearly. These improve empirical support and clarity, although the new normalization-stability finding remains qualitative and lacks a quantitative ablation.
